expectations.text: Defines JWT in plain words (a signed token carrying claims / JSON Web Token) in the same sentence it first appears
expectations.evidence: First sentence: "JWT auth works by having the server issue a signed token instead of a session ID." This describes JWT auth's mechanism rather than defining the noun 'JWT', and 'JSON Web Token' is never spelled out anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Defines 'stateless' in plain words (the server keeps no per-session record) the first time it is used
expectations.evidence: "Any server holding the signing key can verify any valid token independently, with no shared session store and no coordination between servers. That's the stateless property, and it's a real win for horizontal scaling."
